scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-AI-AGENT-AUTO-FIX.statement: The dispute surge is a ticket-handling/response problem, and an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes 'whatever is causing the wrong bills' will resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused more reads to be rejected or substituted with estimates, producing incorrect bills and the dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The nightly MDMS-to-billing handoff (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or failed in August, causing missing/invalid AMI reads that forced estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL.statement: Manual field meter-reading completion dropped (e.g. staffing) in August, increasing missed reads and estimate substitution and thus wrong bills.

H-CS-CAPACITY-SLA-DEGRADATION.statement: The actual rate of billing errors did not change materially; instead CRM response-time/SLA degradation turned normal inquiries into escalated dispute tickets, inflating ticket counts without a change in underlying bill accuracy.

H-TARIFF-CALC-ERROR.statement: A tariff or billing-calculation error affecting bills on ACTUAL meter reads (not just estimate substitution) is a significant, distinct driver of the dispute surge, since the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) were on ACTUAL reads.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field route completion log shows manual meter-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts, meaning a measurable shortfall in manual reads existed during the dispute-surge period that could feed estimate substitution.

Of 3,025 disputed bills, 1,785 were on ACTUAL reads and 1,240 on ESTIMATED reads — actual-read bills are the majority of disputes, not estimate-substituted ones. This means estimate-substitution-based causes (AMI export failure, billing rule change forcing estimates, field read shortfall) can at most explain the smaller (ESTIMATED) share of disputed bills, leaving the larger ACTUAL-read share unexplained by those mechanisms.

The tariff change log shows zero recorded tariff changes, meaning no tariff adjustment event is on record that could explain incorrect bills; this narrows but does not eliminate the broader 'billing-calculation error' hypothesis, since a non-tariff calculation bug could still exist and remains untested, especially for the dominant ACTUAL-read share of disputed bills.

E-04 shows CRM dispute ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, indicating response handling speed is not degraded during the dispute surge.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims there has been no tariff change this year. As a NON_AUTHORITATIVE stakeholder claim it merely corroborates the existing authoritative tool evidence E-03 (tariff change log shows zero records for Aug-Sep 2026) and adds no new information.

CRM dispute volume held near a 590-610/month baseline in Jun-Jul 2026, then jumped to 1180 in Aug and 1260 in Sep — confirming the surge was a sustained roughly 2x increase coinciding with August, not a one-off blip. This quantifies the magnitude/timing of the surge but says nothing about its cause.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a field-reader staffing shortfall (three readers short since July) causes late routes, which produces estimated bills for affected customers — offering a mechanism for the completion shortfall already observed in E-01/F-01. As a NON_AUTHORITATIVE stakeholder claim from a source with a noted bias toward staffing attribution, it corroborates but does not independently verify H-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL, and it still says nothing about the larger ACTUAL-read share of disputes (E-02).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility may only request field route priority changes; execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), formalizing the authority basis already encoded in constraint K-DISPATCH for the push_route_update protected action.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db returns 320 accounts estimated in the last cycle across 40 routes, with only account_id and route fields — no tariff or import-status fields as the work item (W-WI-BILL-RULE-AUDIT-DATA) expected, so it cannot audit the ACTUAL-read billing defect. The count (320) is far smaller than both the 9,200 manual-read shortfall accounts (E-01) and the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-02), suggesting this snapshot covers only one recent cycle rather than the full Aug-Sep dispute window, and it carries no linkage to disputed-bill IDs or read types needed to confirm overlap.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) returns 14 lagging routes each with a completion value (sample: R-00 at 0.70), but the dataset only carries route and completion fields, with no account identifiers. This means the planned join between the 9,200 manual-read shortfall accounts and the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed accounts cannot be performed with this data, mirroring the same missing-join-key gap seen in E-09 on the billing side.

symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a 590-610/month baseline (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) (E-06/F-05).

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume has sustained a ~2x increase since August 2026, from a ~600/month baseline to 1180-1260/month (E-06). The majority of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025) were issued on ACTUAL meter reads, not ESTIMATED ones (E-02), and no tariff change occurred (E-03), so the dominant driver is an unisolated billing-accuracy defect in the billing import/validation step affecting ACTUAL-read bills, not primarily the estimate-substitution pathway (field route completion fell to 0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-01, which can only explain the smaller ESTIMATED-read share); ticket response handling itself remains within SLA (E-04), ruling out a handling-capacity cause.
